application_context.workflow: Agent-proposed MERGE of CRM-ACCT-2097 into canonical CRM-ACCT-1042 after a legal name change
application_context.environment: Synthetic design-time demonstration; no production access
application_context.summary: An agent proposes merging a CRM account created by migration under a company's current legal name into the established master account held under its legacy legal name, relying on a shared official registry ID and a registry-documented name change. The plan assesses the supplied evidence, the approval and authorization conditions and the commit boundary for one protected MERGE.
application_context.temporal_scope: Current account identity as of authorization and commit; legal-name change effective 2024-04-01; registry extract dated 2026-10-15
application_context.persistence_mechanism: PostgreSQL 16.5; customer-required single SERIALIZABLE transaction via MergeCoordinator 2.8.0 with pre-commit validator 1.6; asynchronous outbox consumers after commit

operations.title: Proposed MERGE of CRM-ACCT-2097 into canonical CRM-ACCT-1042 after a legal name change
operations.identity_proposition: CRM-ACCT-2097 (current legal name Northstar Industrial Components Limited) and CRM-ACCT-1042 (legacy legal name Northstar Components Limited) both denote the single continuing legal person with official registry ID FIC-REG-004821, whose legal name changed on 2024-04-01 without change of legal-person identity, for the purpose of one persistent CRM customer-account identity as of the authorization and commit time.
affected_state: UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: accounts - retained canonical row CRM-ACCT-1042 (adoption of the current legal name, row version 18) and the CRM-ACCT-2097 source row (row version 23; its post-merge disposition, such as status flag or tombstone, is not specified); the table is in the customer-declared write set and is required to be in the single SERIALIZABLE transaction, but transaction membership is not proven

UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: account_contact_links - re-association of the three CRM-ACCT-2097 contact links to the canonical account, including handling of duplicate contacts; declared write-set member, transaction membership not proven

UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: account_contract_links - re-association of the two active CRM-ACCT-2097 contracts to the canonical account (six existing on CRM-ACCT-1042); declared write-set member, transaction membership not proven

UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: account_external_ids - external identifiers including registry ID FIC-REG-004821 and the CRM-ACCT-2097 alias; declared write-set member, uniqueness-collision handling and transaction membership not proven
UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: account_merge_history - append-only merge lineage record for this operation; declared write-set member, transaction membership not proven
UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: audit_events - audit record for this operation; declared write-set member, transaction membership not proven
UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: transactional_outbox - outbox event(s) that drive downstream propagation; declared write-set member required to be inserted in the same transaction, membership not proven

UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: storage location for preserved historical legal names and provenance (policy requires preservation); no named table or column is identified, so write-set completeness for this effect is not established

UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: other persistent objects that reference either account ID beyond the seven declared tables (dependent foreign keys, triggers, caches, exports); existence and membership not assessed; historical activity records must retain original account IDs and must not be written
EXTERNAL_OR_ASYNC: CRM search index update performed after commit by an asynchronous outbox consumer (customer-stated)
EXTERNAL_OR_ASYNC: Billing customer read model update performed after commit by an asynchronous outbox consumer (customer-stated)

EXTERNAL_OR_ASYNC: ERP customer crosswalk update performed after commit by an asynchronous outbox consumer (customer-stated); the supplied crosswalk already maps both account IDs to EC-004821, so idempotent handling is required
operations.temporal_scope: Current account identity as of authorization and commit time. The legal-name change took effect on 2024-04-01 per SRC-REG-001 (extract dated 2026-10-15); CRM-ACCT-1042 was created 2019-06-12 under the legacy name; CRM-ACCT-2097 was created 2024-05-15 by migration under the current name. Registry status after the extract date has not been evidenced.
operations.persistence_point: unknown / unverified - HOLD before first persistent write. Customer-required design: one SERIALIZABLE PostgreSQL 16.5 transaction coordinated by MergeCoordinator 2.8.0 covering the seven declared tables and the outbox insertion, with the commit point at that transaction's COMMIT. No evidence proves that the implementation matches this design, that the write set is complete, or that atomicity holds; asynchronous consumers run after commit outside the transaction.
operations.reversibility_basis: No recovery or compensation mechanism (A1), recovery test (A2) or responsible-role attestation (A3) was supplied, and no customer policy accepts non-recovery risk for this operation. Absence of documentation does not prove the merge is not reversible, and ordinary Data Steward / CRM Platform Owner approvals are not acceptance of non-recovery risk. Factual reversibility therefore remains unknown.
operations.classification_note: Production MERGE of persistent shared CRM account identity with downstream propagation: protected IRREVERSIBLE_WRITE path. The label identifies the authorization boundary and does not assert that technical recovery is impossible.

controls.title: Identity proposition and exact official registry ID gate
controls.trigger: A candidate MERGE of CRM-ACCT-2097 into CRM-ACCT-1042 is proposed or re-proposed.
controls.required_action: Require the narrow identity proposition stated for this operation and require an exact official registry ID match (FIC-REG-004821 on both records and in the authoritative registry evidence) plus evidence of legal continuity before the candidate may advance. Registry ID comparison must use a customer-defined, documented normalization rule applied identically to both records and the evidence.
controls.enforcement_point: Candidate preparation and again at pre-persistence evaluation, before any approval request is created.
required_evidence: Exact official registry ID on both records and in the registry evidence
Evidence of legal continuity for the rename interval
Documented registry-ID normalization rule
controls.approval_requirement: None for the gate itself; Data Steward review is separate (CTRL-06).
controls.on_sufficient_support: Advance to the remaining controls; this control alone does not authorize any write.
controls.on_conflict: Block the candidate: do not merge when an official registry ID differs or any record carries a conflicting registry ID.
controls.on_indeterminate: HOLD: ambiguous or non-normalizable registry ID, missing continuity evidence, or an identity proposition that is not exact.
controls.on_failure: Do not persist; route to Data Steward review with the failed check recorded.

controls.title: Similarity-is-not-identity and distinct-registry-ID prohibition (negative control)
controls.trigger: Candidate records resemble each other (names, domains, addresses, contacts, parent/subsidiary or brand relationship) but the evidence does not show the same official registry ID with legal continuity.
controls.required_action: Treat names, domains, addresses and contact similarity as insufficient identity proof. Two records that carry different official registry IDs fail the exact-registry-ID criterion of POL-MDM-07 v3.2 and must not be merged on similarity alone; no approval or authorization path inside this operation can satisfy that criterion, and any exception process would be separate and customer-defined.
controls.enforcement_point: Before evidence promotion and again at the pre-persistence check.
required_evidence: Official registry ID of each record
Corporate relationship evidence retained as a typed relation, not collapsed into identity
controls.approval_requirement: No approval can convert a distinct-registry-ID pair into this MERGE; any exception would be a separate customer-defined process outside this plan.
controls.on_sufficient_support: Not applicable: this control only blocks or holds.
controls.on_conflict: Block the merge and retain the parent/subsidiary or related-entity relation as a typed relation.
controls.on_indeterminate: HOLD pending evidence of the official registry IDs; similarity alone never resolves the case.
controls.on_failure: Do not persist any identity change; record the rejected candidate and reason.

controls.title: Claim-specific evidence eligibility and provenance
controls.trigger: Supplied evidence (registry extract, verification record, agreement, migration report, crosswalk) is to be used to support the identity proposition.
controls.required_action: Admit evidence first as quarantined, promote it only for the specific proposition and role it supports, and record source, proposition, role, temporal applicability, validation basis and validator/policy version. Treat SRC-REG-001 as primary legal-continuity evidence only after its authenticity (SRC-REG-VERIFY-005, a supplied result) is tied to the exact extract and recorded. Treat SRC-LEGAL-002 as corroboration of post-rename name and registry ID. Do not count SRC-MIGRATION-003 and SRC-CROSSWALK-004 as independent identity evidence because they record the customer's own mapping to EC-004821 and share an upstream origin. Do not infer support from absence of a detected conflict.
controls.enforcement_point: Evidence admission and promotion step, before the approval request is created and again at pre-persistence evaluation.
required_evidence: Provenance and validation record IDs per proposition
Verification record tied to the exact extract (hash/identifier) with validator identity and version
Independence assessment of each source
controls.approval_requirement: Evidence eligibility authority is a customer decision (DEC-02).
controls.on_sufficient_support: Mark the proposition supported for the stated scope and interval and continue to the remaining controls.
controls.on_conflict: Keep conflicting observations quarantined for designated adjudication and block the candidate.
controls.on_indeterminate: Keep the observation UNVERIFIED and block the candidate; do not treat repetition or the Planner's own label as support.
controls.on_failure: Do not promote; record the unmet evidence requirement.
controls.owner: Data Steward (customer-stated role) for adjudication; evidence-promotion owner unassigned

controls.title: Temporal continuity applicability and evidence freshness
controls.trigger: The continuity claim relies on a rename effective 2024-04-01 and a registry extract dated 2026-10-15; the authorization and commit occur later.
controls.required_action: Confirm that the continuity evidence applies to the referent and the interval from the rename to the authorization/commit time, that the extract is within a customer-defined freshness limit, and that no dissolution, successor, restructuring or new incorporation is recorded after the extract date. Refresh the evidence when stale or when its age is not covered by a defined freshness limit.
controls.enforcement_point: Pre-persistence evaluation and the immediate pre-write revalidation (CTRL-09).
required_evidence: Customer-defined maximum evidence age
Registry status as of the authorization/commit time
Extract content showing before and after legal names
controls.approval_requirement: Freshness limit is a customer policy decision (DEC-02).
controls.on_sufficient_support: Continue to the remaining controls for the validated interval.
controls.on_conflict: Block and escalate when later registry evidence shows dissolution, succession or a distinct legal person.
controls.on_indeterminate: HOLD or refresh when the freshness limit is undefined, exceeded, or the interval cannot be shown to be covered.
controls.on_failure: Do not persist; require refreshed evidence and a new authorization record.

controls.title: Canonical record and identity-preserving requirements
controls.trigger: The merge direction, resulting names and historical state are determined for the write.
controls.required_action: Retain CRM-ACCT-1042 as canonical and merge CRM-ACCT-2097 into it; never the reverse. After an approved merge adopt the current legal name Northstar Industrial Components Limited on the canonical account while preserving the legacy name and all historical names with provenance; keep CRM-ACCT-2097 resolvable as a source alias; keep historical activity under its original account IDs; append, never update or delete, account_merge_history rows.
controls.enforcement_point: Candidate construction, the in-transaction pre-commit validation, and post-commit validation.
required_evidence: Canonical-record decision per POL-MDM-07 v3.2
Resulting-state specification: names, aliases, links, lineage
Identification of where historical names and provenance are stored
controls.approval_requirement: Approval of the resulting state is covered by CTRL-06.
controls.on_conflict: Block when the merge direction, canonical retention or name adoption contradicts the policy.
controls.on_indeterminate: HOLD when the storage of historical names or the disposition of the CRM-ACCT-2097 row is not specified (DEC-04).
controls.on_failure: Abort before commit; if detected after commit, stop dependent mutations and quarantine (CTRL-13).

controls.title: Separate human approvals bound to the exact operation and state
controls.trigger: The candidate has passed evidence and identity gates and is to be approved for persistence.
controls.required_action: Require two separate human approvals, one from a Data Steward and one from a CRM Platform Owner, each by a different authorized individual and each bound to the exact operation ID OP-DEMO-2026-001, idempotency key demo-merge-1042-2097-v1, source row versions 18 and 23, identity schema CRM-IDENTITY-5, MergeCoordinator 2.8.0, pre-commit validator 1.6, policy POL-MDM-07 v3.2, the promoted evidence set and the declared write set. Any change to a bound item invalidates the approvals. No approval artifacts have been supplied, so no approval exists. These ordinary approvals are not acceptance of non-recovery risk.
controls.enforcement_point: Approval service / MergeCoordinator pre-persistence check and the immediate pre-write revalidation (CTRL-09).
required_evidence: Data Steward approval record bound to operation and state
CRM Platform Owner approval record bound to operation and state
Evidence that the two approvers are distinct and authorized
controls.approval_requirement: Data Steward and CRM Platform Owner, separately (customer policy). Individual identities and the approval record format are not supplied (DEC-01).
controls.on_sufficient_support: Continue to the authorization-path and commit-boundary controls.
controls.on_conflict: Block when a required approver rejects or the approvals disagree on scope.
controls.on_indeterminate: HOLD when an approval is missing, unbound, unverifiable, expired or given by the same individual for both roles.
controls.on_failure: Reject the approval and require a new approval for the current state.
controls.owner: Data Steward and CRM Platform Owner (customer-stated roles)

controls.title: Protected-write authorization path (Path A recovery or Path B accepted non-recovery risk)
controls.trigger: OP-DEMO-2026-001 is a production IRREVERSIBLE_WRITE whose factual reversibility is unknown.
controls.required_action: Hold the write unless exactly one authorization path is established for this operation and its complete production effect scope. Path A requires A1 (documented recovery or compensation mechanism for this exact MERGE and complete effect scope), A2 (successful recovery test on materially equivalent state and schema using current persistence, policy and validator versions) and A3 (attestation by a customer-designated responsible role). When established Path A sets factual reversibility to reversible while the action class stays IRREVERSIBLE_WRITE. Path B is available only when Path A is not established and requires a current explicit customer policy accepting this exact operation's non-recovery risk, operation-specific approval by a role authorized by that policy, and customer-defined separation of duties from the ordinary approvals; it establishes neither reversible nor not_reversible. After Path A is established for the scope Path B is unavailable. An UNMERGE is not recovery for this MERGE unless it independently satisfies A1, A2 and A3. Neither path creates an automatic write.
controls.enforcement_point: Pre-persistence authorization decision and the immediate pre-write revalidation (CTRL-09).
required_evidence: A1 mechanism documentation
A2 recovery-test record with versions
A3 attestation by a designated role
Or: current Path B policy, operation-specific approval, separation-of-duties rule
controls.approval_requirement: A3 attester and Path B approver roles and the separation-of-duties rule are not defined by the supplied policy (DEC-03).
controls.on_sufficient_support: Record the established path and continue to the remaining controls; the path never replaces approvals, evidence or atomicity proof.
controls.on_conflict: Not applicable: path decision does not resolve identity conflicts.
controls.on_indeterminate: HOLD when neither path is fully established or the separation-of-duties question is unresolved.
controls.on_failure: HOLD; a stale Path A claim expires to unknown and does not automatically select Path B.
controls.owner: Unassigned (A3 attester and Path B approver roles to be defined by the customer)

controls.title: Complete write-set and atomicity proof before the first persistent write
controls.trigger: Before any persistent write for the merge begins.
controls.required_action: Prove, with customer-held evidence, that the write set is complete (accounts, account_contact_links, account_contract_links, account_external_ids, account_merge_history, audit_events, transactional_outbox, plus the storage for preserved historical names and any dependent object found by dependency analysis) and that all of it, including outbox insertion, commits in one atomic SERIALIZABLE transaction with a single identified commit point. Prove that no historical activity record or other unlisted object is written. Isolation level alone does not prove atomicity or write-set completeness. If proof is absent, HOLD and begin no write.
controls.enforcement_point: Before the first persistent write, at the MergeCoordinator boundary.
required_evidence: Dependency inventory of objects referencing either account ID
Transaction-boundary evidence for every write-set member
Evidence that triggers and extensions have no effects outside the transaction
controls.approval_requirement: CRM Platform Owner reviews the proof (customer-stated role).
controls.on_sufficient_support: Permit the write to proceed to the remaining controls.
controls.on_conflict: Block when a write outside the declared set or inside historical activity is found.
controls.on_indeterminate: HOLD when completeness, membership or the commit point is unknown or unverified.
controls.on_failure: Do not begin any write; do not start a partial sequence.
controls.owner: CRM Platform Owner (customer-stated role) with application/data owner

controls.title: Immediate pre-write revalidation of record state, schema, coordinator, validator, policy and approvals
controls.trigger: Immediately before any persistent write, including after any delay since approval.
controls.required_action: Revalidate that CRM-ACCT-1042 is still at row version 18 and CRM-ACCT-2097 at row version 23 and both are active, that the identity schema is CRM-IDENTITY-5, the coordinator is MergeCoordinator 2.8.0, the pre-commit validator is 1.6, the policy is POL-MDM-07 v3.2, the evidence and eligibility state and the approvals and authorization-path basis are unchanged and unexpired, and the realized operation exactly matches the authorized operation and write set. Reject a stale authorization and re-evaluate from the evidence stage with a new authorization record; never replay a stale candidate. Retries share one customer-defined retry budget.
controls.enforcement_point: Immediately before the first persistent write, and again inside the transaction before commit.
required_evidence: Current row versions, schema, coordinator, validator and policy identifiers
Authorization record bound to those versions
controls.approval_requirement: New approvals are required whenever a bound item changes (CTRL-06).
controls.on_conflict: Block when current state contradicts the authorized state or evidence.
controls.on_indeterminate: HOLD when a version or state cannot be read or compared.
controls.on_failure: Reject the authorization; require re-evaluation with a new authorization record.

controls.title: Atomic SERIALIZABLE commit and pre-commit abort
controls.trigger: The write is executed after CTRL-01 to CTRL-09 are satisfied.
controls.required_action: Execute every write and the outbox insertion in one SERIALIZABLE transaction. Evaluate the pre-commit validator and the resulting-state invariants inside the transaction before COMMIT, including evidence-to-claim support and the identity-preserving requirements. Commit only on PASS with valid scope and versions. On any failure or serialization conflict before commit, abort the transaction so that no write in any of the seven tables becomes committed; this is a transaction abort, not post-commit compensation. Persist the idempotency key inside the same transaction so that its presence proves the commit.
controls.enforcement_point: In-transaction, immediately before COMMIT, in MergeCoordinator 2.8.0 with pre-commit validator 1.6.
required_evidence: Pre-commit validator result
Transaction identifier and commit evidence
Idempotency key persisted inside the transaction
controls.on_sufficient_support: COMMIT; record audit and outbox events committed in the same transaction.
controls.on_conflict: Abort the transaction and keep the candidate non-persistent.
controls.on_indeterminate: Abort the transaction; the validator or database being unavailable is a failure, not a pass.
controls.on_failure: Abort the transaction and confirm that no committed rows result.

controls.title: Ambiguous commit reconciliation, idempotency and no blind retry
controls.trigger: The commit outcome is unknown (for example the connection is lost around COMMIT) or the same request is received again.
controls.required_action: Do not retry blindly. First reconcile authoritative state by reading, after the failure, whether the idempotency key demo-merge-1042-2097-v1 and the corresponding merge-history, audit and outbox rows exist. Retry only after confirming that the original operation did not commit and that a retry is safe and revalidated under CTRL-09. A duplicate request after a confirmed commit returns the original outcome and performs no second merge. A new authorization record requires a new idempotency key version.
controls.enforcement_point: Immediately after any failure or timeout at or after COMMIT, and at request intake for the idempotency key.
required_evidence: Authoritative read-after-failure result keyed by the idempotency key
Reconciliation record
controls.approval_requirement: None; reconciliation is an automated or operator procedure with a named owner (DEC-05).
controls.on_sufficient_support: If the key is found committed, return the original outcome and continue to post-commit controls.
controls.on_conflict: If partial state is observed, stop and quarantine (CTRL-13).
controls.on_indeterminate: Stay on HOLD until authoritative state can be read.
controls.on_failure: Do not retry; escalate to the reconciliation owner.
controls.owner: Unassigned (reconciliation owner to be named by the customer)

controls.title: Post-commit validation and downstream propagation reconciliation
controls.required_action: Validate the committed state against the authorized operation and write set, then reconcile the asynchronous outbox consumers: CRM search index, Billing customer read model and ERP customer crosswalk. Consumers must be idempotent, tolerate duplicate and out-of-order delivery and tolerate a crosswalk that already maps both IDs to EC-004821. Detect and report divergence between the committed CRM state and each consumer. Stop dependent mutations while a mismatch is unresolved.
controls.enforcement_point: After commit: post-commit validator, outbox consumers and a reconciliation job.
required_evidence: Post-commit validation result
Per-consumer reconciliation result
Outbox delivery and retry records
controls.on_sufficient_support: Record reconciled and mark downstream consistent.
controls.on_conflict: Quarantine on a mismatch between committed state and the authorized operation.
controls.on_indeterminate: Treat unreconciled consumers as inconsistent; do not mark the operation complete.
controls.owner: CRM Platform Owner (customer-stated role) with consumer owners unassigned

controls.title: Post-commit failure, quarantine and recovery
controls.trigger: An invariant fails after commit, an asynchronous effect fails or diverges, or no single atomic boundary can be guaranteed for an effect.
controls.required_action: Stop dependent mutations, reconcile the actual persisted state, and invoke only a documented and tested recovery or compensation procedure for this exact MERGE. If none is established, quarantine the affected accounts and downstream projections and escalate to a named owner while keeping the overall decision on HOLD for further identity changes. Do not claim that a database rollback can reverse a committed or asynchronous effect and do not assume UNMERGE as recovery.
controls.enforcement_point: After commit, on any post-commit validation or reconciliation failure.
required_evidence: Documented tested recovery or compensation procedure (A1/A2) or a quarantine and escalation procedure
Incident and reconciliation record
controls.approval_requirement: Recovery execution requires operation-specific approval under customer policy (DEC-07).
controls.on_sufficient_support: Return to normal once validation and reconciliation pass.
controls.on_indeterminate: Quarantine and escalate; remain on HOLD.
controls.on_failure: Quarantine and escalate; do not retry the merge.
controls.owner: Unassigned (recovery and quarantine owner to be named by the customer)

evidence_requirements.claim: CRM-ACCT-1042 and CRM-ACCT-2097 denote the same legal person identified by official registry ID FIC-REG-004821, which continued across a legal-name change.
required_categories: Authoritative official registry record for FIC-REG-004821
Exact registry-ID match on both CRM records under a documented normalization rule
Evidence of legal-person continuity (registration number unchanged; no dissolution, successor or new incorporation)
Post-rename contracting evidence that corroborates name and registry ID
source_characteristics: Official registry source with traceable provenance and authenticity validation
Scope covering the referent and the rename interval
Corroboration that is independent of the customer's own migration and crosswalk mapping
evidence_requirements.temporal_applicability: Must cover the period from the rename on 2024-04-01 to the authorization and commit time; the extract is dated 2026-10-15.
evidence_requirements.validation_method: Customer promotion process records the proposition, role, provenance, temporal applicability, validation basis and validator/policy version for SRC-REG-001, SRC-REG-VERIFY-005 and SRC-LEGAL-002; the Planner has performed none of these checks.
evidence_requirements.conflict_handling: Any indication of a distinct, successor or dissolved entity, or a differing official registry ID, is a conflict that blocks the merge until adjudicated.
evidence_requirements.unverified_handling: Observations that are not promoted stay UNVERIFIED and are not authorization-eligible; similarity, repetition or Planner confidence is not support.
evidence_requirements.policy_owner: Customer domain-policy owner for POL-MDM-07 v3.2 (named owner not supplied)
gaps: Extract content (before and after legal names, status fields) was described but not supplied.
Contract-side evidence for the six contracts on CRM-ACCT-1042 not supplied.

evidence_requirements.claim: The legal-continuity evidence is temporally applicable: the name change on 2024-04-01 and unchanged legal-person identity apply to the interval through the authorization and commit time with no later dissolution or succession.
required_categories: Registry status as of the authorization/commit time
Rename effective date and continuity statement
source_characteristics: Dated registry evidence with issuer and signature validation
Status information newer than the 2026-10-15 extract when the freshness limit requires it
evidence_requirements.temporal_applicability: From 2024-04-01 to the authorization and commit time. The extract is 37 days older than the run date of 2026-11-21; the customer has not stated a freshness limit.
evidence_requirements.validation_method: Customer-defined freshness check on the registry source at authorization and again at the pre-write revalidation.
evidence_requirements.conflict_handling: A later dissolution, successor, restructuring or new incorporation contradicts continuity and blocks the merge.
evidence_requirements.unverified_handling: Evidence of unknown age is UNVERIFIED for temporal applicability and holds the candidate.
evidence_requirements.policy_owner: Customer domain-policy owner (named owner not supplied)
gaps: Whether the extract states the legacy and current names exactly as on the two records is not evidenced.

evidence_requirements.claim: Both records are active customer-account records of the same entity class at the recorded row versions (18 and 23) under identity schema CRM-IDENTITY-5, and CRM-ACCT-1042 qualifies as the canonical retained record under POL-MDM-07 v3.2.
required_categories: Current record state and row versions
source_characteristics: Authoritative CRM state read at authorization and again before the write
Policy text identifying the canonical-retention rule
evidence_requirements.temporal_applicability: Current state at authorization and at the pre-write revalidation.
evidence_requirements.validation_method: MergeCoordinator pre-persistence read of row versions, status and schema, compared with the authorized values.
evidence_requirements.conflict_handling: A changed row version, status or schema is a stale-state conflict that requires re-evaluation with a new authorization record.
evidence_requirements.unverified_handling: State that cannot be read or compared is treated as unverified and holds the candidate.
gaps: Policy text itself not supplied; only the supplied summary was used.

evidence_requirements.claim: The migration report and the account-to-entity crosswalk, which both map the two CRM accounts to entity EC-004821, are internal mapping records that share an upstream origin and are not independent evidence of identity.
required_categories: Origin and derivation of the EC-004821 mapping
Independence assessment relative to the registry evidence
source_characteristics: Recorded provenance showing whether the mapping derived from the same matching decision
evidence_requirements.temporal_applicability: Mapping created at migration on 2024-05-15; later changes not supplied.
evidence_requirements.validation_method: Customer review of how the mapping to EC-004821 was produced; until then it is context only.
evidence_requirements.conflict_handling: If the mapping contradicts registry evidence (for example a different entity) it is a conflict to adjudicate, not a vote.
evidence_requirements.unverified_handling: Treated as UNRESOLVED_INDICATION or context; never promoted as sole or corroborating support for the identity proposition.
evidence_requirements.policy_owner: Customer domain-policy owner (named owner not supplied)
gaps: Provenance of the EC-004821 mapping not supplied.
Whether the pre-existing crosswalk is correct or itself an earlier unverified resolution is unknown.

evidence_requirements.claim: The complete persistent write set for this MERGE is known and all of it, including the outbox insertion, commits in one atomic transaction with a single commit point, with no write to historical activity or to any undeclared object.
required_categories: Dependency inventory of objects referencing either account ID
Transaction-boundary evidence for each write-set member
Storage location for preserved historical names and provenance
source_characteristics: Customer-held schema, catalog and transaction evidence
Evidence produced in a non-production environment with the same schema, not by a production write
evidence_requirements.temporal_applicability: Applies to the exact schema CRM-IDENTITY-5 and coordinator version 2.8.0 current at authorization and commit.
evidence_requirements.validation_method: Customer-owned dependency analysis and transaction-boundary review; a design-review method is a customer decision.
evidence_requirements.conflict_handling: A write found outside the declared set or inside historical activity contradicts the proposition and blocks the write.
evidence_requirements.unverified_handling: Unproven membership stays UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED and holds the write before the first persistent write.
gaps: Storage location of historical names not stated.
Disposition of the CRM-ACCT-2097 row not stated.

evidence_requirements.claim: An authorization path can be established for this protected MERGE: either Path A (documented, tested and attested recovery or compensation for this exact operation and complete effect scope) or, only if Path A is not established, Path B (explicitly accepted non-recovery risk under current customer policy, operation-specific approval and separation of duties).
required_categories: A2 recovery test record with versions
A3 attestation by a customer-designated role
Or Path B policy, operation-specific approval and separation-of-duties rule
source_characteristics: Operation-specific evidence for this MERGE and its complete effect scope
evidence_requirements.temporal_applicability: Version-bound: valid only while the equivalent state and schema and the persistence, policy and validator versions evidenced by A2 remain current at authorization and commit.
evidence_requirements.validation_method: Customer attestation and approval process; none is supplied.
evidence_requirements.conflict_handling: A stale or failed Path A claim expires to unknown and does not select Path B automatically; an unresolved separation-of-duties question keeps Path B on HOLD.
evidence_requirements.unverified_handling: Unproven A1, A2 or A3, or an unproven Path B policy, approval or separation of duties, holds the write.
evidence_requirements.policy_owner: Unassigned (customer must designate attester and Path B approver roles)
gaps: No recovery mechanism, recovery test, attestation or non-recovery-risk policy supplied.

implementation_points.responsibility: Assemble the candidate operation, bind it to operation ID, idempotency key and versions, run the pre-write revalidation and execute the single SERIALIZABLE transaction.
Quarantine evidence, check conflicts, promote evidence for specific propositions and roles with recorded provenance and validator/policy version.
outputs: Promotion and validation record IDs per proposition

implementation_points.component: Evidence-control record and verification of the registry extract
implementation_points.responsibility: Verify signature and issuer certificate of the extract and tie the result to the exact extract.
outputs: Verification record with validator identity and version

implementation_points.responsibility: Evaluate exact registry ID, continuity, canonical-record and name-adoption requirements and the distinct-registry-ID prohibition.

implementation_points.component: Approval service for Data Steward and CRM Platform Owner approvals
implementation_points.responsibility: Create approval requests, capture two separate approvals bound to operation and state, and invalidate them on change.
implementation_points.owner: Data Steward and CRM Platform Owner (customer-stated roles)

implementation_points.responsibility: Record A1/A2/A3 or the Path B policy, approval and separation-of-duties basis and expire them on version drift.
Validate the resulting state and evidence-to-claim support inside the transaction before COMMIT.
Persist the idempotency key inside the transaction and reconcile unknown outcomes by authoritative read before any retry.

implementation_points.component: Asynchronous outbox consumers (CRM search index, Billing customer read model, ERP customer crosswalk)
implementation_points.responsibility: Apply committed outbox events idempotently after commit.
Compare committed CRM state with the authorized operation and each consumer and report divergence.
Stop dependent mutations, quarantine affected accounts and projections and escalate to a named owner.
Record operation, evidence, approvals, versions, decisions and outcomes.

validation_tests.scenario: Sufficient support under customer policy (hypothetical positive path)
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): the registry evidence for FIC-REG-004821 is authentic, current within the customer's freshness limit, shows the 2024-04-01 name change with unchanged registration number and legal-person continuity, and no dissolution or successor; both records carry the same registry ID under the documented normalization rule.
validation_tests.action: Submit the candidate MERGE of CRM-ACCT-2097 into CRM-ACCT-1042 to the identity and evidence gates.
validation_tests.expected_result: CTRL-01, CTRL-03 and CTRL-04 report support for the stated interval and the candidate advances to the remaining controls. No authorization to write results from this test alone.

validation_tests.scenario: Similarity without sufficient identity support
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): two records share a similar name, domain, address and contacts, but no official registry ID or continuity evidence is attached.
validation_tests.expected_result: The candidate is held; names, domains, addresses and contact similarity are not accepted as identity proof; no persistent write occurs.

validation_tests.scenario: Negative control: parent and subsidiary with different official registration IDs
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): a parent company record and a subsidiary record have near-identical names, the same web domain and address and shared contacts, but different official registry IDs.
validation_tests.action: Submit the candidate MERGE through the same merge gates, with every approval present in the fixture.
validation_tests.expected_result: The merge is blocked on the distinct registry IDs; no approval or authorization path overrides it; the related-entity relation is retained as a typed relation; no persistent write occurs.

validation_tests.scenario: Registry ID equal only after ambiguous normalization
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): the two registry ID values differ in formatting (case, spacing or leading characters) and the customer has not defined a normalization rule.
validation_tests.expected_result: The candidate is held until a documented normalization rule resolves the comparison; no persistent write occurs.

validation_tests.scenario: Material contradiction in registry evidence
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): fresh registry evidence shows a dissolution of the entity or a successor/new incorporation after the 2024-04-01 name change.
validation_tests.action: Submit the candidate MERGE with the new evidence quarantined and adjudicated as a contradiction.
validation_tests.expected_result: The candidate is blocked and escalated for designated adjudication; absence of a conflict is never treated as proof; no persistent write occurs.

validation_tests.scenario: Authenticity of the registry extract indeterminate
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): the verification record cannot be tied to the exact extract (identifier or hash mismatch) or lacks validator identity and version.
validation_tests.expected_result: The extract stays UNVERIFIED and quarantined; it is not promoted as authorization-eligible support; the candidate is held.

validation_tests.scenario: Only non-independent internal mapping evidence
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): the only support is the migration report mapping and the account-to-entity crosswalk, with no registry or contract evidence.
validation_tests.expected_result: The two records are treated as non-independent internal mappings that share an upstream origin; they are not counted as independent corroboration; the candidate is held.

validation_tests.scenario: Temporal mismatch or stale evidence
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): the registry extract is older than the customer's freshness limit, or the freshness limit is undefined, or the evidence does not cover the interval to the commit time.
validation_tests.action: Re-evaluate the candidate at the pre-persistence check.
validation_tests.expected_result: The candidate is held until refreshed registry evidence covers the interval; a new authorization record is required; no persistent write occurs.

validation_tests.scenario: Wrong merge direction or canonical record
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): the candidate attempts to retain CRM-ACCT-2097 as canonical, or to merge CRM-ACCT-1042 into CRM-ACCT-2097.
validation_tests.action: Submit the candidate for pre-persistence validation.
validation_tests.expected_result: The candidate is blocked because POL-MDM-07 v3.2 retains CRM-ACCT-1042 as canonical; no persistent write occurs.

validation_tests.scenario: Resulting-state check fails on name adoption or history preservation
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): the prepared resulting state drops the legacy name, omits provenance of historical names, rewrites historical activity to the canonical ID, or updates or deletes an existing account_merge_history row.
validation_tests.action: Run the pre-commit validator inside the transaction.
validation_tests.expected_result: Validation fails and the transaction aborts with no committed rows in any of the seven tables; the current legal name is adopted only with historical names and provenance preserved.

validation_tests.scenario: Required approvals missing
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): no approval, or only one of the Data Steward and CRM Platform Owner approvals, exists.
validation_tests.expected_result: The operation is held before any persistent write; approvals are not inferred or accepted from the Planner.

validation_tests.scenario: Approval invalid, unbound or replayed on changed state
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): an approval is not bound to the operation ID, idempotency key and state, or both roles were filled by the same individual, or the row version changed after approval.
validation_tests.expected_result: The approval is rejected as invalid and a new approval for the current state is required; no persistent write occurs.

validation_tests.scenario: Path A positive (hypothetical fixture)
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): A1 (documented recovery or compensation mechanism for this exact MERGE and its complete effect scope), A2 (successful recovery test on materially equivalent state and schema using current persistence, policy and validator versions) and A3 (attestation by a customer-designated role) are all established; the write set is complete.
validation_tests.action: Evaluate the authorization path for the operation.
validation_tests.expected_result: Path A eligibility is recorded and factual reversibility becomes reversible for the proven scope while the action class remains IRREVERSIBLE_WRITE; every other control still applies and nothing is written automatically.

validation_tests.scenario: Path A negative: A1 missing or incomplete
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): the recovery mechanism is absent, undocumented, for a different operation, or does not cover the complete effect scope; A2 and A3 are otherwise present.
validation_tests.expected_result: Path A is not established and the operation is held.

validation_tests.scenario: Path A negative: A2 missing, failed, stale or non-equivalent
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): recovery tests are absent, failed, run against non-equivalent state or schema, or predate a change in persistence, policy or validator version; A1 and A3 are otherwise present.
validation_tests.expected_result: Path A is not established and the operation is held.

validation_tests.scenario: Path A negative: A3 attestation missing or invalid
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): the attestation is absent, given by a non-designated role, or does not attest the applicability and results of A1 and A2; A1 and A2 are otherwise present.
validation_tests.expected_result: Path A is not established and the operation is held.

validation_tests.scenario: Path B positive (hypothetical fixture)
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): Path A is not established; a current explicit customer policy accepts this exact operation's non-recovery risk; an authorized role gives operation-specific approval; the customer-defined separation of duties from the ordinary approvals is satisfied.
validation_tests.expected_result: Path B eligibility is recorded; the action class stays IRREVERSIBLE_WRITE and factual reversibility stays unknown; every other control still applies and nothing is written automatically.

validation_tests.scenario: Path B negative: no current policy accepting the non-recovery risk
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): Path A is not established and no current customer policy accepts this exact operation's non-recovery risk.
validation_tests.expected_result: Path B is unavailable and the operation is held.

validation_tests.scenario: Path B negative: approval absent or from an unauthorized role
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): a policy exists but operation-specific approval is absent, not specific to this operation, or given by a role the policy does not authorize; the Data Steward and CRM Platform Owner approvals are present.
validation_tests.expected_result: Path B is unavailable and the operation is held; ordinary approvals do not count as acceptance of non-recovery risk.

validation_tests.scenario: Path B negative: separation of duties absent, unresolved or violated
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): policy and approval exist but separation of duties from the ordinary approvals is not defined, is unresolved, or the same individual gave both approvals.
validation_tests.expected_result: Path B is unavailable and the operation is held.

validation_tests.scenario: Path A and Path B mutual exclusivity
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): Path A is established for the complete effect scope.
validation_tests.action: Attempt to solicit or record acceptance of non-recovery risk for the same operation and scope.
validation_tests.expected_result: Path B is unavailable for that operation and scope; no non-recovery-risk acceptance is solicited or recorded while Path A remains established.

validation_tests.scenario: Write-set completeness or atomicity unverified before the first write
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): no evidence shows that all seven tables, the storage for historical names and the outbox insertion are covered by one atomic transaction with a single commit point.
validation_tests.expected_result: The operation is held before the first persistent write; no partial write sequence starts and isolation level is not accepted as proof of atomicity.

validation_tests.scenario: Write outside the declared set or into historical activity
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): dependency analysis finds an object referencing the account IDs that is not in the declared write set, or the candidate write set includes a historical activity record.
validation_tests.expected_result: The operation is blocked and held until the write set is reconciled; historical activity keeps its original account IDs.

validation_tests.scenario: State, schema, coordinator, validator or policy drift before the write
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): after approval, CRM-ACCT-1042 moves from row version 18 or CRM-ACCT-2097 from row version 23, or the schema, coordinator, validator or policy identifier changes.
validation_tests.expected_result: The authorization is rejected as stale and the candidate is re-evaluated from the evidence stage with a new authorization record; the stale candidate is not replayed.

validation_tests.scenario: Pre-commit invariant failure inside the atomic transaction
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): the pre-commit validator returns a failure or the database reports a serialization conflict before COMMIT.
validation_tests.action: Execute the write inside the single SERIALIZABLE transaction.
validation_tests.expected_result: The transaction aborts and a read of all seven tables shows no committed change from the operation; this is a transaction abort and not post-commit compensation.

validation_tests.scenario: Outbox atomicity
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): a failure is injected after the outbox insertion but before COMMIT, and separately after a successful COMMIT.
validation_tests.action: Execute the write and inspect the outbox.
validation_tests.expected_result: The outbox event exists if and only if the merge committed; no downstream event is emitted for an aborted transaction.

validation_tests.scenario: Ambiguous commit outcome
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): the connection is lost at COMMIT and the outcome is unknown.
validation_tests.expected_result: No blind retry occurs; the authoritative state is read by idempotency key demo-merge-1042-2097-v1; the original outcome is returned if committed; retry is considered only after confirming non-commit.

validation_tests.scenario: Duplicate request after a confirmed commit
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): the merge committed and the same idempotency key is submitted again.
validation_tests.expected_result: No second merge is performed and the original outcome is returned.

validation_tests.scenario: Retry after confirmed non-commit
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): reconciliation confirms the original transaction did not commit and the failure was a serialization conflict.
validation_tests.expected_result: The retry is allowed only after revalidation of state, versions and approvals, within the common retry budget, with a new authorization record if any bound item changed.

validation_tests.scenario: Post-commit validation mismatch
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): after commit the canonical account has a contract or contact link count that differs from the authorized result, or the historical names were not preserved.
validation_tests.expected_result: Dependent mutations stop, the accounts and projections are quarantined, and the overall decision stays on HOLD for further identity changes.

validation_tests.scenario: Downstream consumer failure, duplicate delivery or divergence
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): the search index, Billing read model or ERP crosswalk consumer fails, receives the event twice, or diverges; the ERP crosswalk already maps both IDs to EC-004821.
validation_tests.action: Run outbox consumers and the reconciliation job.
validation_tests.expected_result: Consumers handle duplicates idempotently; divergence is detected and reconciled without re-running the merge; the operation is not marked complete until all consumers reconcile.

validation_tests.scenario: Post-commit failure with no tested recovery procedure
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL FIXTURE (not customer data or evidence): a post-commit failure is detected and no documented, tested compensation procedure for this exact MERGE exists.
validation_tests.expected_result: Dependent mutations stop, affected accounts and projections are quarantined and escalated, the decision stays on HOLD, and UNMERGE is not assumed to be recovery.

planner_checks.setup: A required public reference retrieval is unavailable or a required response field (profile version, requested mutation type or action class, phase) is materially incomplete.
planner_checks.expected_result: Use degraded_reference_unavailable, mark the affected claims unresolved, list the exact missing retrievals and invent no reference-backed content or provenance.

planner_checks.scenario: Reference version drift within one run
planner_checks.setup: Two required retrievals in the same run expose incompatible reference-set versions.
planner_checks.action: Compare version basis and source identifiers and resolve the mismatch.
planner_checks.expected_result: Do not silently combine versions; refresh consistently or mark dependent decisions unresolved or degraded.

planner_checks.setup: The request is not an identity-changing entity-resolution task, for example an unrelated field update.
planner_checks.action: Qualify the request against the Skill scope.
planner_checks.expected_result: State the scope boundary and fabricate no operations, controls or reference coverage.

assumptions.statement: The merge may be difficult or impossible to reverse and is classified as the protected IRREVERSIBLE_WRITE path.
assumptions.basis: A production MERGE changes shared account identity and propagates downstream; no recovery mechanism, test or attestation was supplied.
assumptions.impact: If recovery is later proven through Path A the action class remains IRREVERSIBLE_WRITE and only factual reversibility changes.
assumptions.verification: Customer supplies A1/A2/A3 or a Path B policy (DEC-03).

assumptions.statement: The seven tables named by the customer are the intended write set, and the customer's statement that all writes and outbox insertion must be atomic in one SERIALIZABLE transaction is a requirement, not proof of the implementation.
assumptions.basis: The request states the write set and the required atomicity but supplies no transaction evidence; POL-MDM-07 requires proof before the first write.
assumptions.impact: If the implementation differs, the write set or atomic boundary is wrong and the write must stay on HOLD.
assumptions.verification: Customer dependency analysis and transaction-boundary review (DEC-04).

assumptions.statement: The registry extract, verification record, agreement, migration report and crosswalk say what the request describes; their content was not supplied and none was verified by the Planner.
assumptions.basis: Only descriptions of the evidence were supplied.
assumptions.impact: Different content could change the evidence assessment or reveal a conflict.
assumptions.verification: Customer evidence-promotion process reviews the actual documents (DEC-02).

assumptions.statement: SRC-MIGRATION-003 and SRC-CROSSWALK-004 share an upstream origin and are not independent identity evidence.
assumptions.basis: Both record the customer's own mapping of the two accounts to EC-004821; the derivation of that mapping was not supplied.
assumptions.impact: If the mapping was derived independently from authoritative evidence it could be re-assessed for corroboration.
assumptions.verification: Customer documents the origin of the EC-004821 mapping (DEC-08).

assumptions.statement: The three downstream consumers exist as stated and run after commit, outside the transaction, and read only committed outbox rows.
assumptions.basis: Customer statement; no consumer evidence supplied.
assumptions.impact: Consumer behaviour, ordering or idempotency could differ.
assumptions.verification: Customer consumer owners document idempotency and ordering (DEC-06).

assumptions.statement: The pre-commit validator evaluates the candidate state inside the same transaction before COMMIT, so uncommitted writes are the isolated candidate state for Phase 2 validation.
assumptions.basis: Design mapping from the reference contract to the stated stack; not stated by the customer.
assumptions.impact: If the validator runs outside the transaction the pre-commit abort guarantee does not hold.

assumptions.statement: Only a MERGE operation is in scope; no UNMERGE, SPLIT or staging operation is planned, and no customer requirement for this MERGE is extended to any other mutation type.
assumptions.impact: A separate UNMERGE or staging operation would need its own classification, controls and tests.
assumptions.verification: Customer requests a separate plan if needed.

assumptions.statement: The extract date of 2026-10-15 and the run date of 2026-11-21 make the extract 37 days old; no customer freshness limit applies.
assumptions.basis: Dates supplied or taken from the execution clock.
assumptions.impact: A defined limit could make the extract stale or acceptable.

unresolved_decisions.question: Who are the Data Steward and CRM Platform Owner approvers, what is the approval record format, and how are approvals bound to operation OP-DEMO-2026-001 and its state?
unresolved_decisions.impact: No approval artifacts exist and none were supplied; the operation cannot be authorized.
unresolved_decisions.owner: Customer Data Steward and CRM Platform Owner

unresolved_decisions.question: Which evidence is eligible for promotion for the identity and continuity claims, who decides eligibility, what is the registry-ID normalization rule, what is the maximum evidence age, and does the extract show the legacy and current names exactly?
unresolved_decisions.impact: The identity proposition cannot be treated as authorization-eligible until the customer promotes evidence under a defined policy.
unresolved_decisions.owner: Customer domain-policy owner and Data Steward

unresolved_decisions.question: Is there a documented, tested and attested recovery for this MERGE (Path A), or does a current policy accept non-recovery risk with an authorized approver and separation of duties (Path B)?
unresolved_decisions.impact: Factual reversibility is unknown and the protected write cannot be authorized without exactly one path.
unresolved_decisions.owner: Customer risk owner and CRM Platform Owner

unresolved_decisions.question: What is the proven complete write set and atomic boundary, where are historical names and provenance stored, what is the disposition of the CRM-ACCT-2097 row, and which other objects reference the account IDs?
unresolved_decisions.impact: POL-MDM-07 requires proof before the first write; completeness and atomicity are unproven.
unresolved_decisions.owner: Customer CRM application and data owner

unresolved_decisions.question: How is the idempotency key persisted atomically, what is the retry budget, and who owns ambiguous-commit reconciliation?
unresolved_decisions.impact: Blind retries are prohibited and reconciliation needs an authoritative key and an owner.

unresolved_decisions.question: Are the outbox consumers idempotent and ordered, and who owns downstream reconciliation for the search index, Billing read model and ERP crosswalk?
unresolved_decisions.impact: Post-commit validation and reconciliation cannot be assured without consumer evidence.

unresolved_decisions.question: Who owns quarantine, escalation and any tested compensation after a post-commit failure?
unresolved_decisions.impact: Without an owner and procedure a post-commit failure has no safe path.

unresolved_decisions.question: What is the origin of the EC-004821 mapping in the migration report and crosswalk, and should the crosswalk be reviewed independently of this merge?
unresolved_decisions.impact: The Planner treats these records as non-independent; a reviewed origin could change how they are used. Not blocking because the design does not rely on them.

limitations: This is a design-time plan; no database operation was executed, no record was modified, no production system was accessed and no authorization was granted.
No approval artifacts were supplied, so the operation is not authorized to commit and no approval has been assumed.

The registry extract, verification record, agreement, migration report, crosswalk and policy text were described but not supplied; the Planner had no independent access to the fictional registry and verified nothing.
The reference MCP provided reference requirements and illustrative examples only; it did not assess customer evidence, instantiate policy, issue authorization or return a commit verdict.
No Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema engine was available, so structural schema validation, validator-enforced format checks and the format negative controls were not run.
Proposed tests were designed, not executed; customer runtime tests were not run.

validation_record.validator: No compatible JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 validator was invoked (Python jsonschema not installed; only Ajv 6.15.0, which does not implement Draft 2020-12, was found; network disabled). Supplementary custom Python helper scripts (structural conformance probe and semantic checker) were used; they are not JSON Schema validators.
notes: Design-time plan only. No database operation, production access, approval or authorization occurred.

schema_validation, format_checker_negative_control and validator-enforced format assertion were not run because no Draft 2020-12 engine with format support was available. A custom structural conformance probe (reimplementing a subset of keywords) reported no deviations on the candidate JSON and on the bundled CRM example; it is not a JSON Schema validator and does not substitute for schema_validation.
format_validation is a manual review: a helper script applied RFC 3339 date-time and absolute-URI patterns to every date-time and url value; not schema-engine format assertion.

Semantic checks (custom script): unique IDs, operation/control/test/source/evidence/planner-check references, reciprocal control-test links, operation coverage, explicit OP-ID mentions against operation_ids, chronology, README/JSON consistency including the validation table and readiness fields.
Manual checks: operation classification, authorization-path coverage (nine tests TEST-13 to TEST-21), effect-boundary semantics, MCP provenance and planner checks.
MCP calls in this run used only abstract labels; all call arguments were inspected and contained no customer-specific data. retrieved_at values are the shared run timestamp.
Candidate-stage readiness: not_implementation_ready because blocking customer decisions exist; schema_validation and format_checker_negative_control are unverified.
zip_integrity, customer_runtime_tests and external_client_compatibility were not run. Artifact ledger schema validation and artifact coherence are deferred to the post-freeze sidecar and handoff.
